name: Southeast Chute
descent_text: Descend the chute you climbed. When the snow is continuous, most parties glissade it with an axe in hand, losing roughly 1,000 ft quickly; only do so in control, because a fall on firm or icy snow, or exposed rocks and ice bulges lower down, can injure. If the snow is hard near the top, face in and use crampons for the first part, and in a thaw the surface turns sloppy and post-holes. At the foot of the chute, rejoin the climbers' path through the basin to the timberline junction and follow Trail 812 down to the Upper Trailhead. Late in the season, when the snow runs out, use the summer trail.
approach: Start at the Upper Trailhead (about 3,500 ft) at the end of the spur off FS 24, which needs a Northwest Forest Pass. Trail 812 climbs at once, with stacked switchbacks for the first 0.3 mile before it merges with the lower-trailhead trail near 3,900 ft. Continue up through forest to the signed junction near timberline, about 4,500 ft, where the winter climbers' route leaves the summer trail and goes right. Follow the heavily used footpath along the north fork of Big Creek into the basin below the south-face chute, which is the base of the climb and a usual place for a first break.
overview: Hiking from the lower trailhead covers 6 miles. About a third of the way up, the trail opens onto an avalanche chute, long and straight, rising into the basin below the summit; from there bear SW for the true summit. Use caution on the steep chute and on the last steep section between the basin and the summit, and note abrupt ledges in nearly every direction on the summit. Early in the season the descent gives a superb glissade. Plan on 3.5 to 4 hours to the top; the climb gains about 3200ft.
